# Behavioral research receipts

These sanitized JSON files are data from the authorized investigation, not
implementation examples or production-quality evidence. Nothing triggers requests.

`provenance.json` records original relative paths, SHA-256 hashes and transformations.
Captures are dated 9 October 2026. Originals remain in /tmp/phantom-audio-investigation;
production never reads that directory.

- Round 15: quartets, badge nodes, manifest/cache records, formula failures,
  mute/audio measurements, clip headers, snapshots and parked PubSub results.
- Round 13: catalog slice ID matrix. Consistent numeric-string pseudonyms preserve
  cross-slice overlap for dedupe/coverage checks.

Comment/title text, usernames, request IDs and media URLs are redacted. Context IDs
are pseudonymized. Badge identity/version and public badge images remain evidence.
Do not replay sanitized variables. Quartets retain response_redacted and original
status. The failed mute-overlay record is variable-contract drift, not a usable
operation or a hash-not-found fixture.

Clip continuity establishes matching path/Content-Length and rotated signatures,
not byte hashes. Alignment summarizes 1519 matching durations with a short head
sample. Audio records are measurements, not a binary/full decoder certification.
PubSub's zero messages is a release-exclusion receipt, not an event schema.

Design boundary tests independently as each feature lands. Preserve units,
malformed/partial cases and policy decisions; do not copy investigation tests or
assert narrative overlap percentages.
